authoredNote: Rewritten with the criteria for the colour rules of 7 and 8 October 2026 (brand/colour-rules.json, section 3). The earlier set, ported from the aha-design plugin, graded feedback tints and an app-shell grey body as correct.

evals.prompt: Review a dashboard screen. A plain data panel is styled `.dashboard-panel { background: var(--aha-logo-purple); }` and a summary card is `.summary-card { background: var(--aha-color-primary); }`, described in the pull request as 'coloured for emphasis'. Neither is a state, a highlighted panel, presenting or a viewer. Everything else on the screen is white and token-bound, with no gradients.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C1: a decorative fill on a neutral container.
evals.expected_output: C1 FAILs: two neutral containers are painted purple and Vivid Pink for emphasis; neither is an allowed non-white surface. Fix: remove both fills so the containers inherit white. Overall: NEEDS FIX.

source.why: written with the criteria from brand/colour-rules.json; the plugin judge dataset predates the colour rules of 7 October 2026

evals.prompt: Review an app shell. The layout body behind every page is `.app-body { background: var(--aha-bg-layout); }`, so each page reads as a grey page with white cards on it. Cards are white, there are no gradients, no pale pink and no dark surfaces, and every value is a token.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C2: grey as the page background.
evals.expected_output: C2 FAILs: light grey is the background of the whole page. Grey is allowed only for surfaces inside or beside the white page. Fix: make the layout body white and keep grey for the sidebar, table headers or cards. Overall: NEEDS FIX.

source.why: written with the criteria from brand/colour-rules.json; the plugin judge dataset predates the colour rules of 7 October 2026

evals.prompt: Review a settings page. Three separate panels on the same screen (plan summary, a tip, and an invite prompt) are each styled `background: var(--aha-bg-accent)`. The page is white, hovered rows use the DS list component, there are no gradients and no dark surfaces, and every value is a token.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C3: more than one highlighted panel.
evals.expected_output: C3 FAILs: three pale pink panels on one screen; at most one highlighted panel per screen is allowed. Fix: keep one and make the others white. Overall: NEEDS FIX.

source.why: written with the criteria from brand/colour-rules.json; the plugin judge dataset predates the colour rules of 7 October 2026

evals.prompt: Review a dashboard change. It adds a 'Dark mode' switch to the user menu; when on, `body.theme-dark { background: var(--aha-bg-dark); }` and cards use `var(--aha-bg-dark-raised)`. In the default theme everything is white and token-bound, with no gradients.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.expected_output: C4 FAILs: there is no dark mode, and black backgrounds are for full-screen presenting and video or image viewers only. Fix: remove the dark theme. Overall: NEEDS FIX.

source.why: written with the criteria from brand/colour-rules.json; the plugin judge dataset predates the colour rules of 7 October 2026

evals.prompt: Review an import screen. A failed-import banner is styled `.banner--error { background: var(--import-error-tint); }` where the app defines `--import-error-tint` as a pale red, and a success banner uses a pale green custom property in the same way. Both carry an icon and a sentence. Everything else is white and token-bound.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C5: a tinted status surface.
evals.expected_output: C5 FAILs: status surfaces are tinted red and green. Fix: keep both banners white (the DS alert) and carry the meaning with the icon, the wording and an outline. Overall: NEEDS FIX.

source.why: written with the criteria from brand/colour-rules.json; the plugin judge dataset predates the colour rules of 7 October 2026

evals.prompt: Review a page. The page wrapper is `.page { background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--aha-white), var(--aha-bg-accent)); }` and a promo card is `.cta-card { background: radial-gradient(circle, var(--aha-white), var(--aha-bg-accent)); }`. Neither is the AI border technique: there is no transparent border with a white padding-box fill.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.expected_output: C6 FAILs: both surfaces use a gradient as their fill, and neither is the AI border exception. Fix: use a solid fill. Overall: NEEDS FIX.

source.why: written with the criteria from brand/colour-rules.json; the plugin judge dataset predates the colour rules of 7 October 2026

evals.prompt: Review a list screen on a white page. A hovered row is styled `.row:hover { background: #F7F7F7; }` and a sidebar is `.sidebar { background: #F7F7F7; }`. The grey is the right grey and both surfaces sit inside or beside the white page, but the values are literals. No gradients, no pale pink panels, no dark surfaces.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C7: allowed surfaces, raw values.
evals.expected_output: C7 FAILs: both greys are raw literals. C2 passes because grey is used where it is allowed. Fix: bind `var(--aha-bg-hover)` and `var(--aha-bg-layout)`. Overall: NEEDS FIX.

source.why: written with the criteria from brand/colour-rules.json; the plugin judge dataset predates the colour rules of 7 October 2026

evals.prompt: Review the slide editor. To make it feel on-brand, the editor workspace has a background image of the logo's four hooks, traced by hand as an inline shape and scaled to fill the workspace behind the slide list and the settings panel. The page is otherwise white and grey from tokens, with no gradients.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C8: Splash on the editor, hand-drawn.
evals.expected_output: C8 FAILs: a Splash background on a dense app screen, and the hooks are redrawn by hand. Fix: remove it; a Splash background belongs on an empty state or a hero area and comes from the Background library. Overall: NEEDS FIX.

source.why: written with the criteria from brand/colour-rules.json; the plugin judge dataset predates the colour rules of 7 October 2026

evals.prompt: Review a dashboard. The page and its cards are white (unset). The sidebar is `var(--aha-bg-layout)` and table headers are `var(--aha-bg-container-secondary)`. A selected row is `var(--aha-bg-accent)`, and one 'What is new' panel on the screen is also `var(--aha-bg-accent)`. A failed-import message is the DS alert on white, with an icon and a sentence. There are no gradients, no dark surfaces and no raw colour values.
evals.label: good-control
evals.notes: Control: every allowed non-white surface, used correctly.
evals.expected_output: Every criterion PASSes: white page and cards, grey only beside or inside the page, pale pink for a selected state and one highlighted panel, an untinted status message, no gradients, tokens throughout. Overall: OK TO SHIP.
assertions: Overall verdict is OK TO SHIP

source.why: written with the criteria from brand/colour-rules.json; the plugin judge dataset predates the colour rules of 7 October 2026

evals.prompt: Review two screens. The full-screen presenting view has `background: var(--aha-bg-dark)` behind the slide, and the image viewer overlay does too. The dashboard's empty state (no presentations yet) shows `splash-right-white-16x9.svg` from the Background library behind the heading and the primary button. An AI prompt input has a gradient on its border with a white padding-box fill. Nothing else is non-white.
evals.label: good-control
evals.expected_output: C4 PASSes: black only for presenting and a viewer. C8 PASSes: a library Splash file on an empty state. C6 PASSes: the gradient is the AI border exception. Overall: OK TO SHIP.
assertions: Overall verdict is OK TO SHIP

source.why: written with the criteria from brand/colour-rules.json; the plugin judge dataset predates the colour rules of 7 October 2026

evals.prompt: Review a sign-up page in the product, built as full-width sections stacked down the page: a white first screen, a pale pink section (`var(--aha-bg-accent)`) with the plan comparison, a full white section with the FAQ, then a second pale pink section with the closing call to action. No two coloured sections touch, nothing is a gradient, and every value is a token.
evals.label: good-control
evals.notes: Control: a web page built from full-width sections inside the product may use pale pink sections.
evals.expected_output: C3 PASSes: the page is built from full-width sections, so rules 3.2 to 3.5 apply; the pale pink sections are separated by a full white section and the first screen is white. Overall: OK TO SHIP.
assertions: Overall verdict is OK TO SHIP

source.why: written with the criteria from brand/colour-rules.json; the plugin judge dataset predates the colour rules of 7 October 2026

evals.prompt: Review a read-only report page that a report routine publishes (a weekly dashboard opened from a Slack link, never operated): a row of six <aha-stat-tile look="accent"> number plates in <aha-grid min="160px">, two <aha-chart> charts (a line and a column with a reference line), and an HTML table whose rows alternate white and var(--aha-bg-container-secondary) with 1px dividers and a black semibold header over a 2px Vivid Pink rule. It reflows at 390 px with no horizontal scroll.
evals.label: good-control
evals.notes: Control: a report page is not a product screen; rule 3.11 allows its light grey zebra rows and pale pink plates.
evals.expected_output: C1 and C3 PASS: a report page is a report (environment report-image), where light grey zebra rows and any number of Vivid Pink at 5% plates pass under rule 3.11 and rules 3.2 and 3.7 do not apply. Overall: OK TO SHIP.
assertions: Overall verdict is OK TO SHIP

source.why: colour rule 3.11 extended to read-only report pages (DESY-220)

evals.prompt: Review the Report screen inside the presenter app (people filter and sort responses there) where the KPI cards are all <aha-stat-tile look="accent"> and the response table has zebra rows in var(--aha-bg-accent).
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Contrast: a product Report screen is not a report page; 3.7 still applies.
evals.expected_output: C3 FAILs: this is a screen of the product app, so Vivid Pink at 5% is for hover, selected and one highlighted panel; rule 3.11 covers report images and read-only report pages only. Fix: white tiles (look="plain", at most one accent panel) and plain table rows. Overall: NEEDS FIX.

source.why: colour rule 3.11 extended to read-only report pages (DESY-220)
